text:
Mike: kicking off SEA5 bring-up for mixed A100/H100 GPU pools. Need a rapid QC + oncall signoff before shifting prod routes.

Mike: Quick smoke checklist:
- k8s control plane: all nodes Ready, apiserver p95 < 250ms
- drivers uniform (expect 535.* on all GPU nodes)
- MIG configs validated on H100 nodes; A100s verified for non-MIG workloads
- container runtime sanity: containerd + nvidia-container-toolkit present
- kernel/nv modules: `lsmod | grep nvidia` and `nvidia-smi -L`
- internal artifact proxy reachable for apt/yum/pip
- prefix cache warm + KV cache persistence test
- batcher 95p latency under SLO at target qps
- cross-AZ networking: BGP/route-table + NAT behavior validated
- canary policy: 10% accounts, 5m ramp, watch 99p latency and token error rate
- fallback plan: automatic failover to A100 pool with concurrency cap
- cost gate: compute steady vs burst unit cost per token, compare A100/H100

Ana: networking additions — need egress allowlist to metrics and analytics endpoints, verify NAT ephemeral port capacity, and confirm partner prefix lists for peering.

Samir: SNAT sizing/runbook linked (ops/runbooks/snat-pools). Quick probe I ran:
```
NODE_LIST=$(kubectl get nodes -l gpu -o name)
for n in $NODE_LIST; do kubectl debug $n -it -- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,mig.enabled --format=csv; done
```
Sample: driver 535.102 on H100/A100 nodes, MIG enabled where applicable.

Samir: MIG checks I ran:
- `nvidia-smi mig -lgip` to list configs
- verify pod scheduling maps to MIG slices via `kubectl top pod` and metrics

Tara: SRE guardrails:
- Canary SLO: start at 90% target qps, linear 5m ramp. Abort if 99p latency > 2x baseline over 3 consecutive 1m buckets.
- Pager triggers: GPU ECC error, OOM kills, kernel panics, repeated pod CrashLoopBackOffs (>3 within 10m).
- Prometheus alerts to add: `gpu_memory_pressure`, `gpu_ecc_count`, `container_cpu_usage_seconds_total:rate5m`, `node_net_drops`
- If MIG reconfig fails repeatedly on a node -> cordon+drain automatically with alert.

Mike: auto-routing: do we have an existing policy group that can failover H100 -> A100 -> cpu? Need concurrency cap decrease on failover (recommend -40%).

Samir: yes, `gpu-routing.prod` supports failover chains. I'll open PR to set `concurrency_override: 60%` on failover.

Ana: firewall: allow analytics.int.redwood.io:443 + metrics cluster 10.4.2.0/24. SNAT estimate: ~2.5k concurrent ephemeral sockets at peak -> recommend /22; scheduling nat-loadtest at 03:00Z.

DevBot: scheduled: sea5-snat-loadtest-2026-06-13T03:00Z target 2500 concurrent flows for 10m against NAT gateway.

Tara: dashboards to watch during canary:
- latency by route/model (p50/p95/p99)
- token error rate per 1k tokens
- GPU metrics: mem alloc, utilization, temp, power
- node OOM kills, kubelet evictions, dmesg kernel errors

Mike: Canary plan outline:
1) Warm caches: run synthetic flows 15m at 25% qps
2) Canary: 10% accounts, 5m ramp @90% qps
3) Run chaos probe: kill one GPU pod in each AZ during 10% stage
4) If green: increase to 50% for 10m, monitor
5) Full flip only after cost gate check and post-run notes

Samir: quick smoke commands for oncall:
```
kubectl get nodes -l gpu -o wide
kubectl top nodes --containers | grep nvidia
kubectl logs -n inference pilot-batcher --tail=200
ssh gpu-node-1 'nvidia-smi -q | head -n 80'
```

Ana: cost gating: finance needs per-token steady vs burst calc. If H100 burst unit cost > 2x A100 steady -> restrict burst concurrency and prefer A100 for non-latency-critical routes.

Tara: Explicit rollback criteria:
- 5xx > 1% sustained over 3m
- token error rate > 2x baseline for 5m
- >2 nodes with OOM kills in 10m
- NAT ephemeral port exhaustion signs on gateway

Mike: requesting +1/-1 signoff from oncall and owners. Reply with short reason.

Samir: +1 — validated drivers/MIG and routing exists. Watching kernel/driver alerts.

Ana: +1 — SNAT loadtest scheduled, FW PR open, will monitor egress metrics.

Tara: +1 with reservation: abort if 99p latency breaches SLO during 10% canary; auto-failover to A100 enabled.

oncall-night: ack, will monitor alerts and page if needed.

Mike: thanks. After a successful rollout, update runbook with any deviations, attach cost delta spreadsheet, and file short postmortem if any incidents. Postmortem template: /ops/postmortems/template
